Canada 5Y is only mid-to-high versus its own 5y history; US 5Y is the 99.6th percentile object, so the spread tail is a US-overshoot versus a still-firmer Canada activity/consumer pulse after a hike that was already in the price. That is the condition for using the historical distribution as more than a yardstick: stretch plus a completed, priced catalyst. The 5Y tenor owns the medium-term relative terminal better than 2Y around a just-printed FOMC and better than 10Y (CA-US_10Y 10.60th 5y versus 6.95th for 5Y). attack: Strongest opposing claim is trend-follower: US 2Y, the delivered 16 Sep 25bp hike, and August CPI tightening bias remain aligned, so fading 99th-percentile US yields or a 1-day Canada dip is premature, and CAD should stay lower as the FX inference of that US-outperformance. Verified fact: US 2Y is 4.76 as of 2026-09-18, +9bp 1d / +13bp 5d / +57bp 1m / +57bp 3m, 99.80th 1y. That continuation tape is real.

The claim still does not own CA-US_5Y. Paying US 2Y is an outright US front-end trend. The valuation object is the relative 5Y gap at the 0.20th 1y percentile after a hike that was already >90% priced. A still-rising US 2Y can coexist with Canada remaining too cheap versus the US; it can even be the mechanism that stretched the spread (-12bp 5d / -16bp 1m into the event).

CAD-lower is the weakest opposing FX inference in this bundle. trend-follower themselves call USDCAD a weaker, 1-month-only trend and leave 3m USDCAD down. dollar-king, the dedicated USD-spot seat, will not long USDCAD because WTI 107.02 / 96th percentile and hotter Canadian activity/consumer support CAD. Inference: the USD-higher camp does not have a clean CAD-lower expression.

Canada 5Y -10bp on 17 Sep is the 1-day 'Canada dip' they refuse to fade. That print is why CA-US_5Y sits at a 1y tail, not evidence the 124bp gap is equilibrium. Verified fact: US 5Y 4.86 is 99.60th 1y and 5y; Canada 5Y 3.54 is 97.82nd 1y but only 81.78th 5y. The relative cheapness is a US overshoot versus a still-firmer Canada activity/consumer pulse, not Canada cheap because it fell.

Do not treat the 2Y CA-US shorts in this bundle as opposition. They are the same relative CAD-up / USD-down rates family at a less extreme 1y percentile. Stay in 5Y: it owns the medium-term relative terminal after a just-printed FOMC better than 2Y event noise, and CA-US_10Y is only 10.60th 5y versus 6.95th for 5Y.
defense: Valuation anchor unchanged: CA-US_5Y at executable_marks.rates_rv.CA-US_5Y -124.00000000000003 as of 2026-09-17, 0.198th 1y / 6.95th 5y, z_1y -2.03, after -16bp 1m / -12bp 5d into a Fed hike that was already >90% priced. Convergence belongs in rates RV, not in only-moderately-rich USDCAD.

USD-lower / CAD-higher are relative implications of that spread (economically long US 5Y versus short Canada 5Y), not a spot USD short and not an AUDUSD view. Expression comparison already rejected short USDCAD: 74th 1y / 87th 5y, z_5y 0.99, versus the 5Y spread at a documented dual-horizon tail. Rates remain the cleaner expression under the rates-first mandate.

Why convergence should begin now is still the completed, priced 16 Sep 2026 25bp hike plus residual 1y-tail cheapness. Canada activity 53.2 and consumer 52.5 remain above US 49.92 / 48.5; BoC minutes flag energy pass-through; WTI 107.02 is 96th percentile. The fundamental case for keeping Canada this cheap versus the US is not strengthening.

Canada labor softness is a verified principal risk, not a newly discovered hole. Employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y, unemployment 6.4% versus US 4.1% can justify some of the 124bp gap, as can US core PCE ~3.0% 6m annualized versus Canada trim/median near 2%. That is why paper size stays 20000000 rather than the full 100000000, and why confidence stays 57. It is not why the 0.20th 1y tail is fair after a known hike.
